provenance_note: The reference corpus was authored from SPEC-causeeffect.md and the cited standards without access to this code; this run recomputes every check from the shipping build.
reference: Hand-built cause & effect matrices covering the five spec presets (P1-P5), a clean baseline and one trigger plus one near-miss for each of the 51 review rules CAU-R-001..091 (data validity, opposite-command and trip-versus-permissive conflicts, declared and derived exclusivity with the interval boundary rule and the M_i + M_j > N rule, coverage, safe state, latch and reset, voting independence by device key and by io controller/card/channel, energise/de-energise convention, io fail-state normalisation, bypass provisions, response-time budget, control_functions interlock resolution, analysis method switch at n = 16), scenario sequences for the channel/cause evaluation and the latch/reset acceptance predicate, display-to-SI conversion, matrix-id slug derivation, package item fields, ignored package sections, the mulberry32 check values and two seeded random matrices. Ten further cases (ids prefixed adj-) cover the points spec revision 2026-09-22.2 settled and the ungraded claims the second adjudication pass found. The first four: the spec 3.4 de_energised_state enum, an exclusive pair reached by both the declared and the derived route, the CAU-R-012 target order when the permissive cause is listed first, and the reset refusal reason when two conjuncts of the spec 4.3 predicate fail at once. Expected values were written by hand from SPEC-causeeffect.md rev 2026-09-22.2 and asserted against an own stdlib engine (causeeffect-ref.py); combination counts come from brute force over every subset evaluating the cells directly (spec 4.2), cross-checked against the pairwise count; sampled counts come from an own 32-bit port of mulberry32. Standards clauses are cited as the spec quotes them (IEC 61511-1:2016 10.3.2, 11.8.4, 11.8.5; IEC 61511-1:2003 3.2.45, 11.2.7, 11.6.2, 11.8.3; API RP 14C 7th ed. 4.3.3); the corpus author did not re-read the standard texts, so every rule reference here rests on the spec's formulas. The second pass added six: a bypassed cause that the review still counts (spec 4.4) while the scenario drops it; a 17-cause matrix with analysis.seed 7 and sample_count 1024 and a declared exclusive pair, so that the sampled branch is graded on a seed and a sample count other than the defaults and on rejecting infeasible samples; 'Fail Stopped' and 'stop' normalised to the spec 4.7 'stopped' row, triggering CAU-R-054 on a start effect and missing it on a stop effect; the scenario states running, energised and de-energised; preset P2 with its permissive cell removed, the acceptance-criterion-3 case for CAU-R-011; and the fourteen display units of spec 3.3.1 that conv-display-to-si does not reach.
reference_citations: SPEC-causeeffect.md revision 2026-09-22.3 (the expectations rest on rev 2026-09-22.2; rev 2026-09-22.3 changes no rule and no value, only the §14 list) (_docs/SPEC-causeeffect.md), sections 3-7, 9, 13-15: the normative formulas for every check

IEC 61511-1:2016 Ed. 2.0, 10.3.2 (SRS content: safe state, permissives, energize/de-energize to trip, reset after shutdown, bypasses, dangerous combinations of output states), 11.8.4 (maximum bypass time), 11.8.5 (compensating measures in bypass): clause text as quoted in the spec; not re-read by the corpus author

IEC 61511-1:2003 Ed. 1, 3.2.45 (MooN: 'N independent channels'), 11.2.7 (remain in safe state until reset), 11.6.2 (energize-to-trip circuit integrity), 11.8.3 (operator alerted to bypass): as quoted in the spec
API RP 14C 7th edition (2001) 4.3.3 SAFE chart (each device related to its function in the chart matrix): as quoted in the spec; the origin of the C&E form, basis of CAU-R-020/022

ISO 10418:2019 3rd edition (foreword and introduction, per the spec's 'Sources verified'): offers the prescriptive API RP 14C approach, a structured hazard review, or a combination, and replaced its reproduced SAT/SAC tables by references to API RP 14C; it carries no rule and no case in this corpus, and is listed so that the omission is not read as an oversight.
tolerance: Finding sets (rule@target with severity), verdicts, severity counts, methods, combination counts, exclusive/conflict pair sets, highlighted-cell sets, active cause sets, effect states and reset results: exact, because they are discrete outcomes of boolean formulas. conflict_fraction for n <= 16: relative 1e-12, since it is one division of two exact integers. conflict_fraction for n > 16: |p - 0.25| <= 4*sqrt(0.25*0.75/S) as spec 13 states; the seeded sampled count itself is exact because the mulberry32 draws are bit-reproducible. t_resp: relative 1e-12 (absolute at 0), since it is one addition and one max of stated values. Display-to-SI setpoints: relative 1e-12 against exact rationals (spec 13). No check is marked disputable: the four that were (safe_state none, device_id case, the binary64 response-time sum, AC-3 scope) became graded when spec rev 2026-09-22.2 settled them; the readings still open are recorded in coverage.ambiguities.
